previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 46-year-old woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, gastroparesis, and recurrent abdominal pain was admitted for acute-on-chronic abdominal pain consistent with a gastroparesis flare. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and diffuse abdominal pain, along with hypertensive urgency peaking in the 230s, which improved with pain control. Her admission was complicated by acute kidney injury likely due to prerenal azotemia, which stabilized with IV fluids. A central line was placed for access, and she received antibiotics initially for a positive urinalysis, though these were discontinued due to lack of urinary symptoms. Her diabetes was managed with insulin, and pain was controlled with acetaminophen and tramadol. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans to follow up with gastroenterology for further evaluation of gastroparesis and hematology for chronic leukocytosis and thrombocytosis.

Dear Ms. ___,

We had the pleasure of taking care of you during this admission. 
You were admitted because you had severe abdominal pain and 
nausea, and you were found to have very elevated blood sugars. 
We treated your blood sugars with insulin therapy. Your 
abdominal pain was thought to be due to an acute worsening of 
your existing diabetic gastroparesis. After your sugars were 
better under control, your pain subsided and you were able to 
tolerate your diet without nausea or vomiting. We have set you 
up with outpatient follow up appointments with a primary care 
physician and gastroenterologist at ___. It is very important 
that you follow through with these appointments, as they will 
help you manage your blood sugars and abdominal pain over the

no longer be allowed to schedule appointments at ___.
